content:
maya: Heads up — caught a new OOM pattern on staging during the continuous batching perf test. Not pure slab exhaustion; looks like small fragments accumulate after a kernel switch.
jun: ugh. can you paste the crash logs? which kernel changed? :thinking_face:
maya: root trace and a short nvidia snapshot:
```
OOM: alloc workspace 1.2GiB failed
kernel selected: attention_opt_v3
last kernel before switch: attention_opt_v1
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv,noheader: 12288 MiB
slab_free_bytes: 34 MiB
slab_fragmentation: 18% (growing)
```
maya: also saw many small free slots in the allocator map after reclaim — allocator watermark didn't trigger a coalesce.
alex: hmm that smells like our per-batch ledger not reconciling the transient KV pages that get shadowed during kernel_change. the ledger thinks memory is available but allocator view is fragmented.
sam: timeline? was there a rollout or model switch right before tests?
maya: test script ramped sequence-length distribution up at t+55s; kernel switch happens ~t+60s when avg seq>1024.
jun: can you rerun with trace=alloc and set ENV ALLOC_DEBUG=1? we need the allocation stack for the tiny leftover buffers.
maya: re-ran with alloc trace, snippet:
```
[55.003] allocate(seq_wksp=64KiB) -> slab@0x7f8... size=64KiB
[55.200] free(slab@0x7f8...)
[60.112] kernel_switch: v1 -> v3
[60.115] allocate(reuse_hint=slab@0x7f8...) failed -> split into 8x8KiB fragments
[60.116] allocate(seq_wksp=128KiB) failed -> OOM
```
alex: split-on-reuse is the key. new kernel requests different workspace alignments so we split big free chunks into many small allocations. allocator doesn't coalesce across stripe boundaries.
jun: can we force coalesce on kernel_switch as a short-term mitigation? e.g., run reclaim_coalesce() during the handoff.
sam: would that be expensive? might spike latency.
alex: cheap if we do incremental coalesce limited by time budget: do N buckets per switch, not full compaction. avoids big latency hill.
maya: perf numbers: before patch average p99 latency 48ms, after kernel switch OOM spikes blocked some requests; CPU reclaim took 250ms and killed throughput. test run attached.
jun: ok plan
- short term: add incremental_coalesce(max_ops=256) on kernel switch (low risk)
- mid term: adjust workspace sizing heuristics so kernels prefer power-of-two-aligned reuse boundaries to avoid forced splits
- long term: add ledger->allocator reconciliation job that heals mismatches asynchronously and exposes metrics
alex: agree. i'll open a PR for the incremental coalesce and a followup for heuristics. keeping switch opt v3 disabled in canary for now.
maya: PR would help; tag me for review. also adding a unit test that simulates seq growth and switch to ensure fragmentation stays < 5%.
ci-bot: build queued for branch alex/incremental-coalesce (job #4821)
sam: and we should add a monitoring alert: "fragmentation_ratio > 12% for 30s" so SRE sees this before OOM.
jun: good call. i'll add the alert and a dashboard panel showing free-slab-count over time.
maya: thanks team :thumbsup: will re-run larger matrix after PR merges.
